findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate sentence from one of the two locations, or rewrite each to describe its own section's audit mechanism distinctly.
findings.violation: This exact sentence reappears verbatim under "Special Cases" describing a different team's update process, suggesting a copy-paste duplication rather than two independently verified facts.

findings.evidence: "Also, the benefits team reviews the reimbursement log on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Either remove the superseding-version sentence here or rewrite it to describe what happens to review findings (e.g., "Findings from the most recent review supersede prior ones").
findings.violation: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it" describes version succession for a published document, but the preceding sentence describes a review action, not a publication with versions - the two sentences don't logically connect.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Name the specific clock explicitly (e.g., "the 90-day service requirement" or "the benefit-year eligibility period").
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined anywhere in the document, so it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the benefit-year claim cycle, or something else.

findings.evidence: "Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing."
findings.fix: Rewrite as a simple sequence, e.g., "Once finance confirms the budget line and the manager signs the request, it moves to final processing."
findings.violation: The clause order ("once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line") is garden-pathed and ambiguous about whether the manager signs before or after finance confirms the budget.

findings.evidence: "The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes." followed by "Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Clarify whether there are two distinct confirmations (a pre-submission summary and a post-processing email) or resolve the contradiction into one consistent sequence.
findings.location: How to Apply, second and third paragraphs
findings.violation: These two sentences contradict each other on when confirmation happens - one says confirmation arrives after processing finishes, the other says the employee reviews a confirmation summary before submitting the request.

findings.evidence: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Use consistent units (business days throughout) and specify when the three-day reminder clock starts relative to the two-day review window.
findings.violation: The reminder (three calendar days) occurs after the manager's two-business-day review window already would have elapsed, and the units are inconsistent (business days vs. days), making the sequence of events unclear.

findings.evidence: "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."
findings.fix: Use one consistent term (e.g., "equipment catalog") throughout, or explicitly state that the "approved list" is the catalog.
findings.violation: "Approved list" is introduced here without definition and is never reconciled with the "equipment catalog" referenced elsewhere - it's unclear if these are the same document.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests." followed by "employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: State explicitly whether a photo alone satisfies the one-year retention requirement.
findings.location: Required Documentation, first and second paragraphs
findings.violation: It's ambiguous whether retaining a photo satisfies the one-year retention requirement or whether the physical receipt itself must also be kept.

findings.evidence: "The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year."
findings.fix: Specify explicitly whether the $500 limit is a total per benefit year or applies separately per device category.
findings.violation: Combined with the later statement that the policy applies "per category per employee," it's unclear whether the $500 cap applies per claim, per device category, or as a total across all categories.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person to match the rest of the document, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence shifts to second person ("You," "we") while the rest of the document uses third person ("employees," "the manager"), breaking voice consistency.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee." compared against Eligibility's "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two rules explicitly, e.g., state whether multiple category claims are allowed within the same one-claim-per-year limit or whether categories are each a separate claim.
findings.violation: These two rules conflict - one implies a single claim total per year, the other implies multiple devices are allowed as long as they're in different categories, and neither clause cross-references the other.

findings.evidence: "the stipend item on the request form... the reimbursable item against the request log... the covered purchase amount"
findings.fix: Standardize on a single term throughout, or explicitly define how each term differs from the others.
findings.violation: Three different terms ("stipend item," "reimbursable item," "covered purchase amount") are used for what appears to be the same object/value without clarifying whether they are synonyms or distinct concepts.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days."
findings.fix: Rewrite with an explicit subject, e.g., "The manager countersigns the employee's request within two business days."
findings.violation: The sentence "Countersign the employee request" has no stated subject, so it's unclear who performs the countersigning (manager? finance?), and the passage shifts confusingly from second person ("you") to an imperative with no actor.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as, e.g., "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: The sentence is grammatically malformed - "the uploaded receipt" has no verb and isn't parallel with "confirming eligibility."

findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the equipment catalog after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Reconcile ownership and update cadence into a single consistent statement, or clarify that these are two distinct catalogs/processes.
findings.violation: This contradicts the Program Overview's statement that "the benefits team publishes the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month" - the two sections disagree on who owns the catalog and how often it's updated.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Remove these unrelated sentences from the Program Coordination section.
findings.violation: These sentences are irrelevant to the home-office equipment stipend policy and don't belong in this document.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Integrate the $200 threshold into the Approval Timeline or Reimbursement Amounts section and clarify how it relates to the manager's existing review step.
findings.violation: This introduces a new $200 review threshold that is never mentioned in the Reimbursement Amounts or Approval Timeline sections, leaving the relationship between this review and the manager's two-day approval unclear.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the vendor list on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Define what the vendor list is and how it relates to the equipment catalog, or remove this disconnected closing note.
findings.violation: This repeats the same "supersedes" sentence pattern used in Program Overview, and "vendor list" is a new concept never introduced or connected to the equipment catalog or stipend process elsewhere in the document.
